chapter: Ella, Charlie Christian and Europe with Hayes
title: Americans change in Europe; Germany on Hitler's birthday
summary: He saw the road manager's family behave differently in Europe, and the Germans in Frankfurt treated them kindly, which made him want to leave America.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: But as soon as they arrived in Europe they seemed to be different people, and that's what impressed me so much. I said why should people act one way one place and act differently in another place.
Yeah, since the facts are the same everywhere.

Yeah. Everybody's the same. So I began to realize the phoniness of the profession and the people, and I became aware of how people act, you know, psychologically, and it left a great impression on me, and it made me want to leave America.
Yeah. Oh, yeah. Almost did it. And I was -- we came down to -- well, we were in Frankfurt on Hitler's birthday, and the German people were so beautiful to us it was unbelievable. They were wonderful.
Like I had heard that -- in America -- they wanted the soldiers to fight, and all that. Before they were saying, 'Well, Hitler says you're a bunch of apes.' But that wasn't true.
No. I saw -- at that time an African boy from -- he was Jamaica, a Caribbean boy who was going to school in Heidelberg. He made the highest marks since the foundation of the University.
And I'd see all kinds of Africans going to school in Germany. So I said, 'Now why are Americans saying that Hitler said this when Hitler didn't say a word.'
And, well, all that hypocrisy and everything, it just got me down. You know, because --
